text:
maria_cs: Heads-up — ParcelPay go-live next Tues. They asked for a single-page customer-facing preflight we can share with their infra and product teams. Need it to cover: cache warmup, ideal batch sizes, streaming fallbacks, and a short renewal-risk checklist. Can eng + SRE weigh in on safe defaults?

sam_eng: +1. I can draft defaults for batch/window sizes and a tiny warmup script. Do we want a section with commands they can run against the sandbox?

maria_cs: Yes please. Keep commands copy-paste. Customer is low-latency sensitive (median <200ms). Also include a quick way to smoke-test quality after warmup (sanity prompts).

tyler_sre: For production-safe defaults: start with small warm pool (2 gpus / 4 workers), prefill with 10-20 unique prompt prefixes per tenant, then scale to target concurrency. Batching: recommend a max batch of 16 for 8k context models, 8 for 32k; use dynamic batching by latency SLO.

sam_eng: Draft warmup curl snippet (sandbox):
```
# run 12 warmup requests with varied prefixes
for i in 1..12; do \\  \\
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\  \\
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \\  \\
    -d '{"model":"rwd-8k-latest","input":"Warmup prompt #'$i' for ParcelPay"}' &\\n done\\n wait
```
Use `concurrency` param if they have a tool to parallelize.

june_prod: From product: include a short fallback policy they can show their PMs: primary model -> quantized fallback -> regional fallback -> degraded streaming (partial tokens) with user messaging. Also note cost tradeoffs.

maria_cs: Good. Also add a 3-step \"quality check\" they can run post-warmup: 1) run 5 canonical prompts (we provide 3 sample prompts), 2) check token-latency for each response, 3) verify top-1 output against golden examples.

natalie_cs: I'll add the sample prompts and a mini form they can fill and send back for early renewal signal: basic satisfaction (1-5), hit-rate vs golden, any hallucination flags. Helps tie to renewal risk.

tyler_sre: Add circuit-breaker thresholds: if p95 latency > 500ms for 3 consecutive 5-min windows OR error rate > 2% for 10 minutes, initiate auto-fallback to smaller model + alert CS. Provide command to toggle fallback:
```
# toggle fallback via admin API (example)
curl -X POST https://control.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/parcelpay/override \\  \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_KEY\" \\  \\
  -d '{"fallback_model":"rwd-2k-quant","reason":"latency spike"}'
```

sam_eng: For batching guidance include a tiny table: expected qps -> recommended batch target -> observed latency rough numbers. But keep it one-liner per row, since this is for customers. Example: \"qps <10 -> batch=4 -> median 120ms\".

maria_cs: Nice. Can we also include an optional prefill schedule (cron-style) for low-traffic tenants to keep KV caches primed? e.g., every 15m run 6 warmup prompts during business hours.

tyler_sre: Yup. Suggest: `0,15,30,45 * * * MON-FRI 09-17` run the 6 warmup jobs. Keep total daily warmup <= 1k tokens per tenant to avoid cost surprises.

oncall-bot: reminder: Deploy window for control-plane changes is Thu 02:00-04:00 UTC. Schedule changes to fallback policy must be <= 24h before go-live for audit.

maria_cs: Final ask: Sam + Tyler, can you drop a one-page PDF and the command snippets in #cs-assets by EOD tomorrow? I'll attach the sample prompt sheet and the renewal mini-form.

sam_eng: Yep, will do. I'll keep code blocks minimal and annotated.

tyler_sre: I'll write thresholds + cron example and the quick runbook text for ops.

maria_cs: Thanks team — aiming to send to ParcelPay CS contact Wed morning. :thumbsup:
